hints: Start by recalling the key Contact process equilibrium, oxidation of sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide, and what its mole balance tells you.
Remember that the real catalyst here is vanadium(V) oxide and that any catalyst only speeds up reaching equilibrium, it never changes the yield.
Count the gas moles on each side to see the pressure effect, then think why a modest 1 to 2 atm still gives an excellent conversion.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Contact process equilibrium**

The heart of the process is the reversible oxidation of sulfur dioxide. It is exothermic.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g) \quad \Delta H < 0$$

**Remember what a catalyst really does**

A catalyst provides a faster route with lower activation energy. It speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but the position and yield stay the same.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{catalyst} = \text{V}_2\text{O}_5 \text{ for Contact, Fe for Haber}$$

**Check the effect of pressure**

Look at gas moles: 3 moles on the left, 2 moles on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles, so it favours $\text{SO}_3$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$3 \text{ mol gas} \rightleftharpoons 2 \text{ mol gas}$$

**Link to the conditions used**

About $450^{\circ}\text{C}$ with $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ and 100 to 200 kPa is a compromise for good rate and low cost. Because the equilibrium lies far to the right, the conversion is still very high, around 96 to 98 percent.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ is the correct Contact catalyst, but no catalyst can increase equilibrium yield. It only increases the rate at which equilibrium is reached.
options.B: Incorrect. Pressure does matter here because gas moles change from 3 to 2. Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the right toward $\text{SO}_3$.
options.C: Correct. Under about 450 degrees C and 1 to 2 atm with $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$, the equilibrium lies well to the right. The yield of $\text{SO}_3$ is very high, so only a low pressure is needed.
options.D: Incorrect. Iron is the catalyst for the Haber process for ammonia, not the Contact process. The Contact process uses $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ to increase the rate.
